title: If I Wanted to Make My First $100K in 12 months, I’d Do This

sentences.text: In this video, we're going to go over the five step process that you can follow to build a hundred thousand dollar a year lifestyle business in under 12 months and which you can work through to build a million
sentences.zh: 在本视频中，我们将介绍一个五步流程，你可以遵循它来在12个月内建立一个年收入10万美元的生活方式企业，并通过这个流程在希望大约三到五年内建立一个百万

sentences.text: dollar business in hopefully around three to five years.
sentences.zh: 美元的企业。

sentences.text: So, if you would [music] like a step-by-step process that you can follow, let's dive in.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想要一个可以遵循的逐步流程，让我们开始吧。

sentences.text: All right, so this is what the road map looks like for building your multi-six figure or even low seven figure lifestyle business.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是建立你的多六位数甚至低七位数生活方式企业的路线图。

sentences.text: [music] Over here, we have a line of roughly what revenue is going to be.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们有一条大致表示收入水平的线。

sentences.text: Everyone starts out at zero.
sentences.zh: 每个人都是从零开始。

sentences.text: Over here, we have an inflection point at a hundred thousand dollars a year.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们有一个拐点，年收入10万美元。

sentences.text: Over here, we have a plateau point at around 10 million.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们有一个平台点，大约1000万美元。

sentences.text: Over here, we have 1 million a year.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们有一个年收入100万美元。

sentences.text: Over here is about 3 million a year.
sentences.zh: 在这里，大约是年收入300万美元。

sentences.text: And you can see the graph starts to plateau out around about this level, which highlights the fact that generally lifestyle businesses don't really scale beyond 10 million a year.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到图表在这个水平附近开始趋于平稳，这突出了一个事实，即生活方式企业通常不会扩展到年收入超过1000万美元。

sentences.text: So, if you're okay with that, then we can continue watching this video.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对此没有异议，那么我们可以继续观看这个视频。

sentences.text: And then over here between 100K and a million, we've got about 300,000.
sentences.zh: 然后在这里，从10万到100万之间，我们大约有30万。

sentences.text: And in general, every tripling of a business revenue is when things start to break and when like the paradigm shifts and when like things become a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，企业收入每增长三倍，事情就会开始出问题，范式会转变，情况会变得有些不同。

sentences.text: So, that's why we're sort of dealing in triplings rather than in other kind of units of numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么我们以三倍增长为单位，而不是其他数字单位。

sentences.text: This here is what we call phase five, [music] freedom.
sentences.zh: 这里就是我们所说的第五阶段，[音乐] 自由。

sentences.text: This is where you have true financial freedom because you've got a business that's doing somewhere between 1 million and probably 5 million in revenue.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，你拥有真正的财务自由，因为你的企业收入在100万到500万之间。

sentences.text: Maybe it's somewhere between 50 and 80% margins.
sentences.zh: 利润率可能在50%到80%之间。

sentences.text: So, you can do the math on that.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以自己算一下。

sentences.text: It's a pretty good place to be.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当不错的状态。

sentences.text: Over here, we have phase four, which is leverage.
sentences.zh: 这里，我们有第四阶段，即杠杆。

sentences.text: This is where you're scaling from about a hundred thousand a year to about a million a year.
sentences.zh: 在这个阶段，你从每年大约10万增长到每年大约100万。

sentences.text: And this process takes about two to three years.
sentences.zh: 这个过程大约需要两到三年。

sentences.text: Um some people do it sooner or quicker than that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有些人做得更快一些。

sentences.text: Some people do it like slower than that.
sentences.zh: 有些人做得比那更慢。

sentences.text: This phase, phase five, you kind of hang around in phase five forever.
sentences.zh: 这个阶段，第五阶段，你基本上永远停留在第五阶段。

sentences.text: Because if you have a lifestyle business, then once you hit like the seven figure mark, you actually just kind of want to be hanging out in this range for the longer term.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你有一个生活方式企业，那么一旦你达到七位数大关，你实际上只想长期停留在这个范围内。

sentences.text: And so, really this kind of range here is our ultimate destination.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个范围实际上是我们最终的目标。

sentences.text: We want to become a lifestyle business millionaire.
sentences.zh: 我们想成为一个生活方式企业的百万富翁。

sentences.text: In order to get that, we have to spend a few years in phase four scaling from 100K to a million.
sentences.zh: 为了达到那个目标，我们必须花几年时间在第四阶段，从10万美元扩展到100万美元。

sentences.text: But most of the people watching this video are not yet at 100K yet.
sentences.zh: 但观看这个视频的大多数人还没有达到10万美元。

sentences.text: So, now let's explore the initial three phases.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在让我们探索前三个阶段。

sentences.text: So, we've got phase one, phase two, and phase three.
sentences.zh: 我们有第一阶段、第二阶段和第三阶段。

sentences.text: Phase one is called ideation.
sentences.zh: 第一阶段叫做构思。

sentences.text: Phase two is called validation.
sentences.zh: 第二阶段叫做验证。

sentences.text: And phase three is momentum.
sentences.zh: 第三阶段是动力。

sentences.text: The ideation phase, we ideally want to last around 1 to 2 weeks.
sentences.zh: 构思阶段，我们理想上希望持续大约1到2周。

sentences.text: The validation phase generally lasts about 1 to 3 months.
sentences.zh: 验证阶段通常持续大约1到3个月。

sentences.text: And then the momentum phase, generally 6 to 12 months, depending on how much work you put into it.
sentences.zh: 然后是动力阶段，通常6到12个月，取决于你投入了多少工作。

sentences.text: So, if we're doing this well and we are stacking the unfair advantages that we have, it's actually fairly doable getting from 0 to 100k a year in [music] business revenue, which is an $8,333 a month run rate.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们做得好，并且叠加我们拥有的不公平优势，从0到年收入10万美元的音乐业务收入实际上是相当可行的，这相当于每月8333美元的运行率。

sentences.text: And it's fairly doable getting there within 12 months if you do the right things and if you willing to put in the [music] work.
sentences.zh: 如果你做正确的事情并且愿意投入工作，在12个月内达到这个目标是相当可行的。

sentences.text: I'm going to say that overall our goal here is about 12 months to go all the way from 0 all the way through to 100k a year.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，我们总的目标是在大约12个月内从0一路走到年收入10万美元。

sentences.text: When I first did this journey, it took me 2 years to go from 0 to 100k, but I knew nothing.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次走这条路时，我花了2年时间从0到10万美元，但我当时什么都不知道。

sentences.text: I'd never read any books about business.
sentences.zh: 我从未读过任何关于商业的书。

sentences.text: There was no videos about entrepreneurship.
sentences.zh: 当时没有关于创业的视频。

sentences.text: And if I knew what I knew now, I'd probably be able to speed run that journey in probably about 3 months even if I had no audience as long as I had the skills that I have.
sentences.zh: 如果我知道我现在所知道的，我可能能够在大约3个月内快速完成这段旅程，即使没有观众，只要我拥有我所拥有的技能。

sentences.text: I have a bunch of friends who've made that journey.
sentences.zh: 我有一群朋友走过这段旅程。

sentences.text: Some of them have gotten there within like 3 months.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人在大约3个月内就达到了目标。

sentences.text: Some of them have gotten there within 6 months.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人在6个月内就达到了这个目标。

sentences.text: Some of them 12 months.
sentences.zh: 一些人在12个月内。

sentences.text: So, I think 12 months is a good kind of middle-of-the-road target to shoot for.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为12个月是一个不错的中间目标。

sentences.text: Obviously, some people are going to get there way quicker and some people are going to take a bit longer to get to 100k a year.
sentences.zh: 显然，有些人会更快达到，而有些人则需要更长的时间才能达到年收入10万美元。

sentences.text: So, within phase one, we have two key milestones.
sentences.zh: 在第一阶段，我们有两个关键里程碑。

sentences.text: The first one is we figure out what is our niche.
sentences.zh: 第一个是确定我们的细分市场。

sentences.text: And once we have figured that out, the next thing we need to do is we need to figure out what is our offer.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们确定了这一点，接下来我们需要确定我们的产品。

sentences.text: And this is a first draft offer.
sentences.zh: 这是初稿产品。

sentences.text: Niche answers the question of who am I helping and what am I helping them with.
sentences.zh: 细分市场回答了“我在帮助谁以及我在帮助他们解决什么问题”的问题。

sentences.text: And then the offer answers the question of what am I actually trying to sell to them.
sentences.zh: 而产品则回答了“我实际上想向他们销售什么”的问题。

sentences.text: And the reason it's a first draft is because in this phase, we're spending 1 to 2 weeks doing a bunch of brainstorming, doing a bunch of research, maybe talking to AI to come up with a niche and an
sentences.zh: 之所以说是初稿，是因为在这个阶段，我们会花1到2周进行大量的头脑风暴、研究，或许还会与AI交谈，以提出一个细分市场和

sentences.text: offer.
sentences.zh: 产品。

sentences.text: But it's only when we put it out into the market to validate the offer that this becomes a more solidified offer.
sentences.zh: 但只有当我们将其推向市场以验证这个方案时，它才成为一个更稳固的方案。

sentences.text: And then we get to the single hardest part of the entrepreneurship game, the least fun part, which is validation.
sentences.zh: 然后我们进入创业游戏中最困难的部分，最无趣的部分，即验证。

sentences.text: And what we are trying to do there is we are trying to get our first sale.
sentences.zh: 我们试图在那里做的是获得我们的第一笔销售。

sentences.text: So, until you get a customer to actually give you money for the thing, all of this niche and offer, it's all theoretical.
sentences.zh: 所以，在客户真正为你的东西付钱之前，所有这些利基市场和方案都只是理论上的。

sentences.text: You need someone to give you money to validate your business idea.
sentences.zh: 你需要有人给你钱来验证你的商业想法。

sentences.text: In between this process of like coming up with a first draft offer [music] and getting our first sale, what we're going to be doing is we're going to be taking a bunch of discovery calls.
sentences.zh: 在提出初稿方案和获得第一笔销售之间，我们要做的是进行大量的探索性通话。

sentences.text: We are going to be speaking to people in our target market and we're going to be doing some market research on those calls and we're going to be trying to understand what their problems are and pitching them or
sentences.zh: 我们将与目标市场的人交谈，在这些通话中进行一些市场调研，试图了解他们的问题，并向他们推销或

sentences.text: presenting them our offer and then refining the offer based on feedback.
sentences.zh: 向他们展示我们的方案，然后根据反馈完善方案。

sentences.text: Because then once we have a first sale, we're now in great territory, we're now in momentum mode.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦我们有了第一笔销售，我们就进入了良好的状态，进入了动力模式。

sentences.text: Well, now it's just a case of like scaling from first sale to 10K in revenue, from there to 30K in revenue, and then it's not too bad getting to 100K revenue.
sentences.zh: 那么，现在就是从第一笔销售扩展到1万美元收入，再从那里到3万美元收入，然后达到10万美元收入并不太难。

sentences.text: 100K revenue a year is really only about $8,300 a month.
sentences.zh: 年收入10万美元实际上每月只有约8300美元。

sentences.text: So, if you are selling something for let's say $3,000, you only need three clients a month in order to hit 100K range.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你以3000美元的价格出售某物，你每月只需要三个客户就能达到10万美元的范围。

sentences.text: If you're able to sell a retainer package for let's say $2,000 a month, you only need four or five clients period to actually get to the 100K a year rate because you're selling a recurring like retainer package.
sentences.zh: 如果你能销售一个每月2000美元的预聘套餐，你实际上只需要四五个客户就能达到年收入10万美元，因为你销售的是经常性预聘套餐。

sentences.text: Of course, if you're selling cheap things like $10 ebooks or $27 courses or you know, template packs or anything like that, you need to get more sales in order to get these sorts of numbers, which is why I'm
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你销售的是便宜的东西，比如10美元的电子书、27美元的课程或模板包之类的，你需要获得更多销量才能达到这些数字，这就是为什么我

sentences.text: generally an advocate of recommending that you sell expensive things rather than cheap things.
sentences.zh: 通常主张推荐你销售昂贵的东西而不是便宜的东西。

sentences.text: Okay, so let's start by zooming into phase one where we are figuring out our niche and our first draft offer ideally within one to two weeks.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们从聚焦第一阶段开始，在这一阶段我们确定我们的利基市场和初步报价，理想情况下在一到两周内完成。

sentences.text: The thing to keep in mind here is that if you want to start a business and you want to make money in any way, you only make money if you solve problems for someone else who's willing to pay
sentences.zh: 这里要记住的是，如果你想创业并以任何方式赚钱，你只有在为愿意付钱的人解决问题时才能赚钱。

sentences.text: you to solve that problem.
sentences.zh: 你来解决那个问题。

sentences.text: All money is given to you in exchange for simply solving problems.
sentences.zh: 所有的钱都是作为解决问题的交换而给予你的。

sentences.text: Now, the first step here is to figure out our niche.
sentences.zh: 现在，第一步是确定我们的利基市场。

sentences.text: What a niche is it is this this sort of overlap between a group of people and a problem.
sentences.zh: 什么是利基市场？它是人群和问题之间的这种重叠。

sentences.text: And the overlap between the group of people and the problem that they have is known as a niche.
sentences.zh: 人群和他们所面临的问题之间的重叠被称为利基市场。

sentences.text: For example, with my first successful business back in the day, the people I was serving was students applying to medical school in the UK.
sentences.zh: 例如，我早年第一个成功的业务中，我服务的对象是申请英国医学院的学生。

sentences.text: And the problem I was helping them solve was that I was helping them prepare for the BMAT, which was this like medical admissions exam.
sentences.zh: 我帮助他们解决的问题是准备BMAT，这是一种医学入学考试。

sentences.text: So, they were a group of people who had a problem and they were willing to pay me to teach classroom courses teaching them how to ace this exam [music] so that they could get into med school.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们是一群有问题的人，愿意付钱让我教他们如何通过考试，以便进入医学院。

sentences.text: of my friends, Sahel, he has software that helps video editors.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友萨赫尔，他有一个帮助视频编辑的软件。

sentences.text: They are the people with the problem that video editing takes too damn long.
sentences.zh: 他们是有问题的人，问题就是视频编辑太耗时了。

sentences.text: And so, video editors are willing to pay him for his software that helps to speed up video editing.
sentences.zh: 因此，视频编辑愿意付钱给他，购买他的软件来加速视频编辑。

sentences.text: The way you make money is by solving problems for people who are willing to pay to have those problems solved.
sentences.zh: 赚钱的方式就是为那些愿意付钱解决问题的人解决问题。

sentences.text: And that is the first thing that we really need to figure out with our business.
sentences.zh: 这是我们真正需要弄清楚的第一件事。

sentences.text: Now, how do you figure this out?
sentences.zh: 那么，如何弄清楚这一点呢？

sentences.text: Well, there's a lot of different things you can do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有很多不同的方法可以尝试。

sentences.text: Um the way that I recommend you do it is, firstly, you identify what are your craft [music] skills.
sentences.zh: 我推荐的方法是，首先，确定你的专业技能是什么。

sentences.text: I.e., what personal or professional expertise do you already have that could help someone solve some kind of problem?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你已经拥有哪些个人或专业专长，可以帮助他人解决某种问题？

sentences.text: You want to ask yourself, what are the things that you're good at?
sentences.zh: 你要问自己，你擅长什么？

sentences.text: What's the stuff on your CV?
sentences.zh: 你的简历上有什么？

sentences.text: What is your current employer actually paying you to do, right?
sentences.zh: 你现在的雇主实际上付钱让你做什么？

sentences.text: If you've solved problems in your personal life, if you were overweight at one point and then you managed to lose weight, like one of my friends does like this stoic weight loss type thing where he helps basically overweight
sentences.zh: 如果你在个人生活中解决过问题，比如你曾经超重然后成功减肥，就像我的一个朋友那样，他做一种类似斯多葛式减肥的事情，帮助那些超重的人

sentences.text: people solve the problem of weight loss.
sentences.zh: 解决减肥问题。

sentences.text: He's got the personal experience at having lost a load of weight himself, and so now he's able to help other people solve that problem.
sentences.zh: 他自己有成功减掉大量体重的亲身经历，所以现在他能帮助其他人解决这个问题。

sentences.text: So, what you want to do is you want to make a list of your craft skills.
sentences.zh: 所以，你要做的是列出你的手艺技能。

sentences.text: What are the skills or expertise or experiences that I already have?
sentences.zh: 我已经拥有哪些技能、专长或经验？

sentences.text: Because starting a business based on pre-existing skills means that you can get to you can get to this 100k year mark a lot quicker.
sentences.zh: 因为基于已有技能创业意味着你可以更快地达到年收入10万美元的目标。

sentences.text: That's not to say you have to have pre-existing skills.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你必须有现成的技能。

sentences.text: It is totally possible to enter a brand new niche and then figure out what problems they have and then develop the skills to solve those problems.
sentences.zh: 完全有可能进入一个全新的领域，找出他们的问题，然后培养解决这些问题的技能。

sentences.text: But, life becomes easier and quicker if you're trying to make money if you are serving a niche that is served by skills that you already have, rather than skills that you have to learn from scratch.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你服务的领域与你已有的技能相匹配，而不是需要从头学起的技能，那么赚钱会更容易、更快。

sentences.text: Essentially, what we want to do is we want to make a long list of people and problems that we could potentially help using our craft skills.
sentences.zh: 本质上，我们要做的是列出一长串我们可以利用手艺技能帮助的人和问题。

sentences.text: The way we do this for our students in the Lifestyle Business Academy is we ask them to come up with a list of 15 to 20 potential niches.
sentences.zh: 我们在生活方式商业学院为学生做的方法是，让他们列出15到20个潜在的细分领域。

sentences.text: The way this looks like is we give them like a worksheet type of thing where there's like a table.
sentences.zh: 看起来是这样的：我们给他们一个类似工作表的东西，里面有一个表格。

sentences.text: Um >> [music] >> there is a column that says person, like who is the person, what is their problem, what is your promise.
sentences.zh: 嗯 >> [音乐] >> 有一列写着“人”，比如这个人是谁，他们的问题是什么，你的承诺是什么。

sentences.text: And then, we ask three questions.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们问三个问题。

sentences.text: I have to give a shout out to one of my mentors, Toki More, for giving me these three questions cuz these [music] are great in terms of like narrowing down a niche and those three questions are do I
sentences.zh: 我必须感谢我的一位导师Toki More，因为他给了我这三个问题，因为这些问题在缩小利基市场方面非常棒，这三个问题是：我

sentences.text: like them, can I actually help them, and will they be happy to pay?
sentences.zh: 喜欢他们吗？我真的能帮助他们吗？他们愿意付钱吗？

sentences.text: [music] And generally what I recommend for our students is you ask yourself will they be happy to pay at least $2,000 because again life becomes easier when you're trying to build a business getting to a 100k a year
sentences.zh: [音乐] 通常我推荐给学生的做法是，问自己他们是否愿意支付至少2000美元，因为当你试图建立业务并达到年收入10万美元

sentences.text: and beyond if you are selling expensive things and I define expensive as about $2,000 or above.
sentences.zh: 甚至更高时，如果你卖的是昂贵的东西，生活会变得更容易，而我把昂贵定义为大约2000美元或以上。

sentences.text: You can certainly get rich selling cheap things it just takes longer.
sentences.zh: 当然，卖便宜的东西也能致富，只是需要更长时间。

sentences.text: So this is an excerpt from one of our workbooks where you can see we've got person problem promise like help and pay.
sentences.zh: 这是来自我们工作手册的一段摘录，你可以看到我们有“人、问题、承诺”，比如“帮助”和“支付”。

sentences.text: For example, the people could be chiropractors, their problem could be not enough customers and so the promise that our business delivers is we help them get more customers.
sentences.zh: 例如，这些人可能是脊椎按摩师，他们的问题可能是客户不足，所以我们业务提供的承诺是帮助他们获得更多客户。

sentences.text: And then we're ranking like help and pay in terms of red, yellow, and green.
sentences.zh: 然后我们根据“帮助”和“支付”进行红、黄、绿评级。

sentences.text: Red is like no definitely not.
sentences.zh: 红色表示绝对不行。

sentences.text: Yellow is kind of like maybe and green is like oh yeah definitely.
sentences.zh: 黄色有点像可能，绿色则是哦对，当然可以。

sentences.text: So in this context do I like chiropractors?
sentences.zh: 那么在这种情况下，我喜欢脊椎按摩师吗？

sentences.text: Uh not really.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不太喜欢。

sentences.text: Can I help them get more customers?
sentences.zh: 我能帮他们获得更多客户吗？

sentences.text: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.text: Will they pay?
sentences.zh: 他们会付钱吗？

sentences.text: Well, yes they'll definitely pay because like it's a business and we're helping them make more money so that one's easy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，他们肯定会付钱，因为这是一个生意，我们帮他们赚更多钱，所以这个很容易。

sentences.text: And so what we want to do is we want to get good at problem hunting because again business is about solving problems for people who willing to pay to have those problems solved.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想做的是善于发现问题的狩猎，因为再次强调，商业就是为那些愿意付钱解决问题的人解决问题。

sentences.text: So a by starting with our craft skills but then also by thinking what are the sort of people and problems that we are already familiar with.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先从我们的手艺技能开始，然后也要思考我们已经熟悉哪些类型的人和问题。

sentences.text: Let's say you've worked in tech and so you're quite familiar with other people working in tech and also probably the customers of your tech company.
sentences.zh: 假设你在科技行业工作过，那么你对其他在科技行业工作的人很熟悉，可能也熟悉你科技公司的客户。

sentences.text: You would then be trying to figure out what problems do those people have that I could potentially solve.
sentences.zh: 然后你会试图弄清楚那些人有什么问题是我可能解决的。

sentences.text: And what you want to do is try and generate around 15 to 20 different niche ideas.
sentences.zh: 而你想做的是尝试产生大约15到20个不同的细分市场想法。

sentences.text: [music] The reason we want to do that is because generally when it comes to niche selection we want to start out it's sort of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: [音乐] 我们想这样做的原因是，通常在选择细分市场时，我们一开始会做类似这样的事情。

sentences.text: It's a three-step process I think of as diverge, converge, and emerge.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个三步过程：发散、收敛和涌现。

sentences.text: This by the way is a general principle for creativity in almost every every field and is the exact concept that we have on these like fancy pens that we've designed with Baronfig diverge converge emerge anyway.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这是几乎所有领域创造力的通用原则，也正是我们与Baronfig合作设计的这些精美笔上所体现的概念：发散、收敛、涌现。

sentences.text: This very much applies to niche selection because diverge is like we're thinking very broad and we're thinking divergently about the 15 20 ideally even more potential niches we could serve.
sentences.zh: 这非常适用于细分市场选择，因为发散意味着我们思考得非常广泛，发散性地思考15、20甚至更多潜在的细分市场。

sentences.text: We are then following a process to converge on like our gold silver, bronze, our top one, two, and three [music] niches.
sentences.zh: 然后我们遵循一个过程，收敛到我们的金、银、铜牌，即我们的前三名细分市场。

sentences.text: And usually in the process of doing that, the correct niche emerges over time.
sentences.zh: 通常在这个过程中，正确的细分市场会随着时间的推移而涌现。

sentences.text: And then we pick a niche, we stick to it for a while, we develop expertise within a niche, we craft an offer within that niche, we do validation within that niche, we serve customers within that niche, and then
sentences.zh: 然后我们选择一个细分市场，坚持一段时间，在该细分市场中发展专业知识，在该细分市场中打造产品，进行验证，服务客户，然后

sentences.text: we have a successful business that gives us fun, freedom, and flexibility to live life on our own terms.
sentences.zh: 我们就拥有一个成功的业务，它给我们带来乐趣、自由和灵活性，让我们按照自己的方式生活。

sentences.text: Oh, by the way, if you are enjoying this video and you haven't yet subscribed to the channel, um you might like to.
sentences.zh: 哦，顺便说一句，如果你喜欢这个视频并且还没有订阅频道，嗯，你可能会想订阅。

sentences.text: It's completely free.
sentences.zh: 完全免费。

sentences.text: I think you click on my channel name and you hit the subscribe button, and then you're more likely to see stuff like this.
sentences.zh: 我想你点击我的频道名称，然后点击订阅按钮，这样你就更有可能看到类似的内容。

sentences.text: Plus, it lets me know that you like this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 另外，这让我知道你喜欢这类内容。

sentences.text: Once you figure out your niche, you then have to come up with a first draft offer.
sentences.zh: 一旦你确定了你的细分领域，你就必须提出一个初稿提案。

sentences.text: So, your niche answers the question of who do I help and what do I help them with?
sentences.zh: 所以，你的细分领域回答了这个问题：我帮助谁，以及我帮助他们做什么？

sentences.text: Your first draft offer answers the question of what do I think I want to actually sell to them.
sentences.zh: 你的初稿提案回答了这个问题：我认为我想实际向他们销售什么。

sentences.text: Crucially, you are not building any kind of product yet.
sentences.zh: 关键是，你还没有构建任何类型的产品。

sentences.text: We need to understand the difference between an offer and a product.
sentences.zh: 我们需要理解提案和产品之间的区别。

sentences.text: Let's take my book, for example.
sentences.zh: 以我的书为例。

sentences.text: The product is the book itself.
sentences.zh: 产品就是书本身。

sentences.text: It is the text in the book, the writing in the book, etc., etc. But the offer is the packaging of the book.
sentences.zh: 它是书中的文字、书中的写作等等。但提案是书的包装。

sentences.text: It is the title, it's the subtitle, it's the world's most followed productivity expert, it's the quote from Mark Manson.
sentences.zh: 它是书名、副标题、世界上最受关注的效率专家、马克·曼森的引语。

sentences.text: The stuff at the front and the back of the book is the offer.
sentences.zh: 书前面和后面的内容就是提案。

sentences.text: When someone goes to the bookstore or goes on Amazon to buy the book, they are not actually buying the product.
sentences.zh: 当有人去书店或上亚马逊买书时，他们实际上买的不是产品。

sentences.text: They are buying the offer, and then what they get is the product.
sentences.zh: 他们买的是提案，然后他们得到的是产品。

sentences.text: Now, the mistake that a lot of noob entrepreneurs make is that they will jump to building the product before validating that people even want the offer.
sentences.zh: 现在，许多新手创业者犯的错误是，他们在验证人们是否想要这个产品之前，就急于构建产品。

sentences.text: And it would be such a tragedy if you spent three years writing a book only to then realize that no one wants to read it.
sentences.zh: 如果你花了三年时间写一本书，结果却发现没人想读，那将是一个巨大的悲剧。

sentences.text: This is, in fact, the single biggest reason why most businesses fail.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这正是大多数企业失败的最主要原因。

sentences.text: [music] At least in the early days, they are trying to sell something that no one actually wants.
sentences.zh: 至少在早期，他们试图销售一些实际上没人想要的东西。

sentences.text: So, you really do not want to take the approach of build it and they will come.
sentences.zh: 所以，你真的不应该采取“先构建，他们就会来”的方法。

sentences.text: You instead want to create an offer, which takes like a day because it's not that hard coming up with a title and a subtitle and like a elevator pitch.
sentences.zh: 相反，你应该创建一个产品方案，这只需要一天时间，因为想出一个标题、副标题和电梯演讲并不难。

sentences.text: And then you present the packaging of the thing to your prospects, and you see if they're interested.
sentences.zh: 然后，你把产品的包装呈现给你的潜在客户，看看他们是否感兴趣。

sentences.text: And if lots of people are like, "Oh my god, that sounds amazing.
sentences.zh: 如果很多人反应：“哦，天哪，这听起来太棒了。

sentences.text: Sign me up."
sentences.zh: 算我一个。”

sentences.text: and are willing to pay you money for the thing before you've even built [music] it, that is when you know you have demand.
sentences.zh: 并且愿意在你还没有构建产品之前就付钱给你，那时你就知道有需求了。

sentences.text: That is when you know you have a viable business.
sentences.zh: 那时你就知道这是一个可行的生意。

sentences.text: But you really do not want to be building first.
sentences.zh: 但你真的不应该先构建产品。

sentences.text: This is an a thing that I wish would get into the heads of more people who are trying to start businesses.
sentences.zh: 这是一件我希望更多想创业的人能明白的事情。

sentences.text: You want to validate your offer first [music] before you try and build the product.
sentences.zh: 在尝试构建产品之前，你应该先验证你的报价。

sentences.text: Now, the offer is made up of what I call the six P's.
sentences.zh: 现在，报价由我所说的六个P组成。

sentences.text: We have person.
sentences.zh: 我们有“人”。

sentences.text: Who is the person who is the absolute center of your bull's eye?
sentences.zh: 谁是那个绝对处于你靶心中心的人？

sentences.text: The way to think about this is like let's say this is a dartboard.
sentences.zh: 思考这个问题的方式是，假设这是一个飞镖盘。

sentences.text: And >> [music] >> this this is your kind of your niche, right?
sentences.zh: 而这就是你的利基市场，对吧？

sentences.text: It's sort of like the people and problem that you're solving for, which we figured out in step one.
sentences.zh: 这有点像你在第一步中确定的你要解决的人群和问题。

sentences.text: In the offer step, what you're trying to do is you're trying to define who is at the absolute center of the bull's eye.
sentences.zh: 在报价步骤中，你要做的是定义谁处于靶心的绝对中心。

sentences.text: Now, that's not to say these are the only customers you serve.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说这些是你服务的唯一客户。

sentences.text: But, like if you're throwing darts, you're going to be aiming for the bull's eye.
sentences.zh: 但是，就像扔飞镖一样，你会瞄准靶心。

sentences.text: I mean, in reality you're going to be aiming for triple 20, but let's forget that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上你会瞄准三倍20分，但让我们忽略这一点。

sentences.text: Let's assume you're going to be aiming for the bull's eye and like some of your shots are going to hit on the bull's eye, but you know, they might land here or here or here or here or here
sentences.zh: 假设你要瞄准靶心，虽然有些箭会正中靶心，但你知道，它们可能落在这里、这里、这里、这里或这里

sentences.text: or there or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或者那里，或者其他地方。

sentences.text: By aiming for the bull's eye, you actually end up landing somewhere on the dartboard.
sentences.zh: 通过瞄准靶心，你最终会落在飞镖盘的某个位置。

sentences.text: So, what we are trying to do is define who do we think is the absolute dream client, our perfect future client, the customer that will absolutely benefit from the thing that we potentially want to sell and who has
sentences.zh: 所以，我们要做的是定义谁是我们认为的绝对理想客户，我们完美的未来客户，那个会从我们可能想要销售的东西中绝对受益并且有

sentences.text: the money to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 钱来支付的人。

sentences.text: Once we figure out the person, we sketch out details about the problem.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们确定了这个人，我们就勾勒出问题的细节。

sentences.text: Like what is the problem that they have and [music] why is it really painful?
sentences.zh: 比如他们有什么问题，以及为什么这个问题真的很痛苦？

sentences.text: We want to sketch out the pain.
sentences.zh: 我们想要勾勒出痛苦。

sentences.text: Pain is not one of the six P's.
sentences.zh: 痛苦不是六个P之一。

sentences.text: Maybe it could be.
sentences.zh: 也许它可以是。

sentences.text: It could be a seven P's.
sentences.zh: 它可以是七个P。

sentences.text: Once we've defined a person and problem in more detail because we kind of knew that from our niche, we then come up with a promise.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们更详细地定义了人物和问题（因为我们从细分市场中已经大致了解），我们就提出一个承诺。

sentences.text: Now, the promise is like less than 10 words that explains what we actually do.
sentences.zh: 现在，承诺就是少于10个词，解释我们实际做什么。

sentences.text: And the goal of the promise is to [music] be sufficiently intriguing to the person with a problem that they want to find out more.
sentences.zh: 承诺的目标是足够吸引有问题的个人，让他们想了解更多。

sentences.text: So, for example, let's take my lifestyle business academy, which is sort of like our online business school.
sentences.zh: 例如，以我的生活方式商业学院为例，它有点像我们的在线商学院。

sentences.text: The person we're targeting is like the corporate professional who's got skills, they've got expertise, they're probably earning over 100K a year, they're probably living in the US or maybe the UK.
sentences.zh: 我们针对的是拥有技能和专长的企业专业人士，他们可能年收入超过10万美元，可能住在美国或英国。

sentences.text: And the problem that they have is that they feel unfulfilled and they feel a lack of freedom and flexibility in their life.
sentences.zh: 他们的问题是感到不满足，生活中缺乏自由和灵活性。

sentences.text: They maybe like the idea of traveling and being able to work remotely, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们可能喜欢旅行和能够远程工作的想法，诸如此类。

sentences.text: What they're optimizing for is freedom.
sentences.zh: 他们追求的是自由。

sentences.text: And so then our promise is we'll help you build a $100,000 a year lifestyle business in under 12 months.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的承诺是帮助你在12个月内建立一个年收入10万美元的生活方式企业。

sentences.text: Now, for that particular audience who has that particular problem, that is an That's a compelling promise.
sentences.zh: 对于有那个特定问题的特定受众来说，这是一个有吸引力的承诺。

sentences.text: And that is what you want in your promise.
sentences.zh: 这就是你想要的承诺。

sentences.text: You want it to be just sufficiently intriguing.
sentences.zh: 你希望它足够引人入胜。

sentences.text: Now, of course, once they get into the program, then I give all the caveats that like, "Okay, well, the 12 months depends on you doing 10 to 15 hours a week of work, and like there's this whole process
sentences.zh: 当然，一旦他们加入项目，我会给出所有警告，比如“好吧，12个月取决于你每周工作10到15小时，而且还有整个过程。”

sentences.text: you have to follow, and then if you don't follow the process, it's going to take longer than that, and like, you know, you got to do what we tell you, and we're going to support you, and blah blah
sentences.zh: 你必须遵循这个过程，如果你不遵循，那就会花更长时间，而且，你知道，你得按我们说的做，我们会支持你，等等等等。

sentences.text: blah blah blah."
sentences.zh: 等等等等。

sentences.text: But, in the promise stage, no one cares about the details.
sentences.zh: 但是，在承诺阶段，没人在乎细节。

sentences.text: No one cares about the caveats.
sentences.zh: 没人在乎那些附加说明。

sentences.text: The promise just needs to be compelling enough that they want to find out more.
sentences.zh: 承诺只需要足够吸引人，让他们想了解更多。

sentences.text: The promise for FireCut, which is, you know, my friend's a hell's video editing software, the person is video editors, the problem is editing takes too long, and so the headline promise is something like, "Save 4 hours in every
sentences.zh: 对于FireCut来说，你知道，这是我朋友的一款视频编辑软件，用户是视频编辑者，问题是编辑耗时太长，所以标题承诺是类似“每次视频编辑节省4小时”这样的。

sentences.text: single video edit."
sentences.zh: 每次视频编辑节省4小时。

sentences.text: Like that promise is intriguing enough for video editors for them to want to find out more.
sentences.zh: 这样的承诺对视频编辑者来说足够有趣，让他们想了解更多。

sentences.text: Okay, so once we've figured out our promise, our prospect is now sufficiently intrigued they want to find out more.
sentences.zh: 好了，一旦我们确定了承诺，我们的潜在客户就足够感兴趣，想了解更多了。

sentences.text: This is when we tell them the plan.
sentences.zh: 这时我们告诉他们计划。

sentences.text: [music] Now, the way we can think about this is that let's say we've got a person, and they are in a sad situation, and we want to get them into a happy situation.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们可以这样想：假设有一个人，他处于糟糕的处境，我们想让他进入快乐的处境。

sentences.text: >> [music] >> Let's say, I don't know, they're unfulfilled in their job, and they want to build a lifestyle business.
sentences.zh: 假设，我不知道，他们对工作不满意，想建立一种生活方式型生意。

sentences.text: One way of thinking about this is like they're on this cliff over here, they want to get across to that cliff over there, but there's this like enormous chasm [music] between these two cliffs, which they cannot cross by
sentences.zh: 一种思考方式是，他们在这边的悬崖上，想要到达那边的悬崖，但两座悬崖之间有一个巨大的鸿沟，他们无法跨越

sentences.text: themselves, or if they could, it would be treacherous, and it would be difficult to navigate.
sentences.zh: 靠他们自己，或者即使能跨越，也会非常危险且难以导航。

sentences.text: What our business is trying to do [music] is basically build a bridge for them.
sentences.zh: 我们的业务试图做的，基本上就是为他们建造一座桥梁。

sentences.text: We're like, "Hey, come along into my business, and we're going to build a bridge for you that will take you from A to B."
sentences.zh: 我们说：‘嘿，加入我的业务，我们将为你建造一座桥梁，带你从A到B。’

sentences.text: And this is what we can think of as the plan.
sentences.zh: 这可以看作是计划。

sentences.text: The promise is telling them is promising them like what's the dream destination.
sentences.zh: 承诺就是告诉他们，向他们承诺梦想的目的地。

sentences.text: And then the plan is like, "Okay, well, step one, step two, and step three."
sentences.zh: 而计划就是：‘好的，第一步，第二步，第三步。’

sentences.text: It's the three or four or five-step process that we'll follow with them to get them to the destination.
sentences.zh: 这是我们将与他们一起遵循的三步、四步或五步流程，以到达目的地。

sentences.text: We still haven't built our product yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有构建我们的产品。

sentences.text: We still haven't really talked about the product.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有真正讨论产品。

sentences.text: We haven't talked about the stuff the the stuff they get.
sentences.zh: 我们还没有谈论他们得到的东西。

sentences.text: What we are giving them is the plan, assuming they're intrigued enough by the promise.
sentences.zh: 我们给他们的是计划，假设他们对承诺足够感兴趣。

sentences.text: [music] So, for example, in our context with the Lifestyle Business Academy, the plan we give them is that, "Hey, it's a three-step plan to get you from zero to 100k.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，在我们的生活方式商业学院的背景下，我们给他们的计划是：“嘿，这是一个三步计划，让你从零到10万。”

sentences.text: Phase one is ideation, phase two is validation, phase three is momentum, blah blah blah blah blah blah.
sentences.zh: 第一阶段是构思，第二阶段是验证，第三阶段是动力，等等等等。

sentences.text: And what we want to get is buy-in from them about the plan.
sentences.zh: 我们想要的是他们对这个计划的认可。

sentences.text: We want them to have the clarity that if they follow the plan, they're able to get to the promise.
sentences.zh: 我们希望他们清楚，如果他们遵循这个计划，就能实现承诺。

sentences.text: Once we have gotten buy-in on our plan, at that point, we talk about the product, if we want to.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们获得了对计划的认可，那时我们才谈论产品，如果我们想的话。

sentences.text: This is like what you actually get.
sentences.zh: 这就是你实际得到的东西。

sentences.text: Like with our academy, it's like you get one-on-one Slack support anytime you want.
sentences.zh: 就像我们的学院，你可以随时获得一对一的Slack支持。

sentences.text: There's coaching clinics on niches and offers and content and sales that are happening every day.
sentences.zh: 每天都有关于细分市场、产品、内容和销售的辅导诊所。

sentences.text: There's like a weekly workshop run by Ali that blah blah blah blah blah blah.
sentences.zh: 还有由Ali主持的每周研讨会，等等等等。

sentences.text: There's like you get this fancy workbook that blah blah blah.
sentences.zh: 你还会得到一本精美的练习册，等等等等。

sentences.text: You know, it's the stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是这些东西。

sentences.text: But the mistake people make when they're creating a business is that they over fixate on the product.
sentences.zh: 但人们在创业时犯的错误是，他们过度关注产品。

sentences.text: And what we need to understand is that the prospect, or your hopefully hopeful future customer, doesn't actually care about the product.
sentences.zh: 我们需要理解的是，潜在客户，或者说你希望成为未来客户的人，实际上并不关心产品本身。

sentences.text: What they care about is the transformation that the product is going to get them.
sentences.zh: 他们关心的是产品能带给他们的转变。

sentences.text: And instead of giving them more stuff, they would ideally like less stuff.
sentences.zh: 而且，与其给他们更多的东西，他们更希望得到更少的东西。

sentences.text: Back in the day, the way you would sell like let's say a course would be like there's 300 hours of content in this course and 58 different templates and this that and the other.
sentences.zh: 在过去，销售比如一门课程的方式会是：这门课程有300小时的内容、58个不同的模板等等。

sentences.text: That just doesn't work anymore because no one's got time.
sentences.zh: 这种方法现在已经行不通了，因为没人有时间。

sentences.text: Like we're already overloaded with content.
sentences.zh: 我们已经 overloaded 了内容。

sentences.text: People would much rather get to the transformation, get to the destination, get to the promised land.
sentences.zh: 人们更愿意直接到达转变、到达目的地、到达应许之地。

sentences.text: They would much rather get that with a course that has only two hours of content rather than a course that has 200 hours of content.
sentences.zh: 他们更愿意通过一门只有两小时内容的课程来实现这一点，而不是一门有200小时内容的课程。

sentences.text: Worrying about what's in the product only comes once you've nailed your person, you figured out the problem, you found a compelling enough promise, you found a plan that like high-level actually gets them to the promise.
sentences.zh: 只有当你确定了目标人群、找到了问题、找到了足够有说服力的承诺、找到了一个高层面上能实现承诺的计划之后，才需要考虑产品里有什么。

sentences.text: And now we can figure out what's the stuff, the deliverables, the things we need to add to our product in order to execute on the plan.
sentences.zh: 现在我们可以确定需要添加到产品中的东西、可交付成果以及执行计划所需的内容。

sentences.text: Once we figure that out, this is where we figure out our price.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们确定了这些，我们就可以确定价格了。

sentences.text: And again, my recommendation is that you charge at least $2,000.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，我的建议是至少收费2000美元。

sentences.text: A lot of people at this point are like, "Oh my god, I can't imagine charging $2,000 for anything."
sentences.zh: 很多人在这个时候会说：‘天哪，我无法想象为任何东西收费2000美元。’

sentences.text: And to which I would say like, "Okay, fair enough."
sentences.zh: 对此我会说：‘好吧，有道理。’

sentences.text: But like let's have a little bit more creativity.
sentences.zh: 但让我们多一点创造力。

sentences.text: Let's see if we can find a person who has enough money and a problem that's painful enough for them to pay $2,000 for it.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看能否找到一个有足够钱并且问题足够痛苦的人，愿意为此支付2000美元。

sentences.text: But once you have sketched out your first draft offer in person, problem, promise, plan, product, price, you turn it into a kind of one-pager.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你草拟了你的第一版提案——人物、问题、承诺、计划、产品、价格——你就把它变成一页纸。

sentences.text: And now congratulations, you have graduated the ideation phase and you're and you are now ready to actually see if there is a market for your idea.
sentences.zh: 现在恭喜你，你已经完成了构思阶段，准备好真正看看你的想法是否有市场了。

sentences.text: At this point with our students in the Lifestyle Business Academy, we give them feedback on the one-pager.
sentences.zh: 此时，在生活方式商业学院，我们会给学生们关于这一页纸的反馈。

sentences.text: We have like this list of like checklist that they go through to make sure that like the the promise makes sense and like all of this funky stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个清单，他们逐项检查，确保承诺合理以及所有那些花哨的东西。

sentences.text: At this point, one thing you should definitely do is read Alex Hormozi's book 100 million dollar offers.
sentences.zh: 此时，你绝对应该做的一件事是阅读Alex Hormozi的《1亿美元报价》这本书。

sentences.text: It's really, really good and you can run it through the value equation and you can, you know, just basically follow the step-by-step process in his book.
sentences.zh: 这本书非常好，你可以通过价值方程来运用它，基本上按照他书中的步骤一步步来。

sentences.text: But the key point I want to make is that coming up with an offer is actually not hard because you haven't had to talk to any customers yet.
sentences.zh: 但我想说的关键是，想出一个报价其实并不难，因为你还没有和任何客户交谈过。

sentences.text: You haven't had to do anything.
sentences.zh: 你还没有做任何事情。

sentences.text: You're just like doing the paperwork.
sentences.zh: 你只是在做文书工作。

sentences.text: It's really not that hard to just run this process of [music] just figure out what are some problems you could solve for some people and then just read 100 million dollar offers, follow the process of the six P's
sentences.zh: 运行这个过程真的不难，[音乐] 只需找出你可以为一些人解决哪些问题，然后阅读一亿美元的报价，遵循六个P的过程。

sentences.text: and just try and come up with some a few first draft offers.
sentences.zh: 然后尝试想出一些初稿报价。

sentences.text: Going through this process will then give you a firmware update on how to come up with business ideas.
sentences.zh: 经历这个过程会让你对如何想出商业创意进行一次固件更新。

sentences.text: Like even if you don't have any ideas right now and you just sort of pretend follow this process to come up with the first draft offer for like a random thing.
sentences.zh: 即使你现在没有任何想法，只是假装遵循这个过程，为某个随机的事情想出一个初稿报价。

sentences.text: I'd say, I want to help people in Hong Kong who've got a problem of like they don't want to walk their dog and I'm going to help my promise is going to be I will walk your dog for
sentences.zh: 我会说，我想帮助香港那些有不想遛狗问题的人，我的承诺是我会帮你遛狗。

sentences.text: you.
sentences.zh: 你。

sentences.text: It's like, okay, that's kind of random, but like sure, let's just craft a pretend first draft offer just to get in the reps, to get in the experience of seeing what it actually takes to craft an offer for
sentences.zh: 这有点随机，但好吧，我们只是假装制作一个初稿报价，只是为了练习，为了体验真正制作一个报价需要什么。

sentences.text: something.
sentences.zh: 某事。

sentences.text: Oh, by the way, quick thing.
sentences.zh: 哦，顺便说一句，快速的事情。

sentences.text: If you're enjoying this video and you want to find out more about our mentorship program, the Lifestyle Business Academy, there's a link down below to the wait list so you can totally sign up to the wait list.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个视频，想了解更多关于我们的导师计划——生活方式商业学院，下面有一个等待名单的链接，你可以完全注册到等待名单。

sentences.text: So anyway, at this point, we have our niche and we have a first draft offer and hopefully this has taken less than two weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，此时，我们有了我们的细分市场和一个初稿报价，希望这花了不到两周时间。

sentences.text: Unfortunately, we do have some students in our academy that overthink this process despite how much we try and help them not overthink the process and kind of like the graph we show them is like this is like how
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我们学院里确实有一些学生过度思考这个过程，尽管我们尽力帮助他们不要过度思考，而且我们给他们看的图表就像这样，这是关于

sentences.text: much thinking you do when it comes to your business idea.
sentences.zh: 你在商业想法上投入了多少思考。

sentences.text: This is like and this range is one to two weeks.
sentences.zh: 这就像，这个范围是一到两周。

sentences.text: If you spend less than about a week, mostly our students have like full-time jobs and stuff so like they're putting in 10 to 15 hours a week.
sentences.zh: 如果你花的时间少于大约一周，我们的学生大多有全职工作之类的，所以他们每周投入10到15个小时。

sentences.text: So maybe like 10 hours.
sentences.zh: 所以大概10个小时。

sentences.text: If you're spending any less than around that time thinking about your offer, it's probably not enough time.
sentences.zh: 如果你花在思考你的产品上的时间少于那个时间，可能时间不够。

sentences.text: This is probably under-thinking when it comes to your niche and offer cuz it is like a really important part of the business.
sentences.zh: 这可能是对你的利基和产品思考不足，因为这是业务中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.text: This is the sweet spot, but then over here, we have over-thinking.
sentences.zh: 这是最佳点，但在这里，我们有过度的思考。

sentences.text: Yes, the niche and the offer is really, really important and it is the foundation of your business, but it is all theoretical until it comes into contact with the market, and that is what happens in phase two, validation.
sentences.zh: 是的，利基和产品非常重要，是业务的基础，但在与市场接触之前，一切都是理论性的，而这正是第二阶段——验证——所发生的事情。

sentences.text: Now, the validation stage, as we talked about, can often take 1 to 3 months, sometimes less than that, sometimes a bit more than that, just again, just depending on how much work you put into it.
sentences.zh: 现在，验证阶段，正如我们所说，通常需要1到3个月，有时更短，有时更长，这取决于你投入了多少工作。

sentences.text: And the goal of validation is to validate our offer.
sentences.zh: 验证的目标是验证我们的产品。

sentences.text: To validate, is there actually a market for people that actually want to pay for this thing that we have theoretically constructed on a Google Doc.
sentences.zh: 验证，是否真的存在一个市场，有人愿意为我们理论上在Google文档上构建的东西付费。

sentences.text: Now, basically, the way the validation process works, we want basically have at least 10 discovery calls.
sentences.zh: 现在，基本上，验证过程的工作方式是，我们至少要有10次探索性通话。

sentences.text: Ideally, ideally 30, maybe even more than that, but ideally 10 discovery calls.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，理想是30次，甚至更多，但理想是10次探索性通话。

sentences.text: And these are 10 calls where we are presenting our offer to someone who's genuinely in the in the target market for that particular offer.
sentences.zh: 这10次通话中，我们向真正处于该特定产品目标市场的人展示我们的产品。

sentences.text: So, we got our niche, we got our offer, and now we're going to have these 10 different conversations with people, and as a result of the conversations, we are going to refine our offer.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们有了细分市场，有了产品，现在我们要进行这10次不同的对话，通过这些对话，我们将完善我们的产品。

sentences.text: There's this phrase in the military that no plan survives first contact with the enemy.
sentences.zh: 军事上有句话：没有计划能在第一次与敌人接触后幸存。

sentences.text: The idea being is that like, sure, you can theory craft a plan all you like, but like, once once you actually get into the arena, things are going to change.
sentences.zh: 意思是，当然，你可以随心所欲地理论构建计划，但一旦真正进入竞技场，情况就会改变。

sentences.text: Similarly, I like the phrase that no offer survives first contact with the market.
sentences.zh: 同样，我喜欢这句话：没有产品能在第一次与市场接触后幸存。

sentences.text: We can do all the work we theoretically like to come up with the best first draft offer, but until we put it in front of real people who actually have the problem that we think we're solving, and we
sentences.zh: 我们可以理论上做所有工作来提出最好的初稿产品，但直到我们把它放在真正有我们认为正在解决的问题的人面前，并且我们

sentences.text: are able to present our offer to them to get their feedback, and maybe even to try and land a sale, until we do that, we won't actually know if our offer is any good.
sentences.zh: 能够向他们展示我们的产品以获得反馈，甚至尝试达成销售，直到我们这样做，我们才能真正知道我们的产品是否好。

sentences.text: This is why the validation process is in many ways the most important part about starting a business.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么验证过程在某种程度上是创业最重要的部分。

sentences.text: It's also the hardest.
sentences.zh: 这也是最难的部分。

sentences.text: It's where you have the maximum amount of imposter syndrome because you have no idea if your offer's any good.
sentences.zh: 这是你冒名顶替综合症最严重的时候，因为你不知道你的产品是否好。

sentences.text: You haven't yet made any sales, and so you're still sort of in the red in terms of you've invested some time and maybe some money into the process.
sentences.zh: 你还没有任何销售，所以从投入的时间和可能的金钱来看，你仍然处于亏损状态。

sentences.text: You haven't yet made a return, and you're having to go and talk to people and sort of present your offer to them to see if they would actually want to buy the thing.
sentences.zh: 你还没有获得回报，你必须去和别人交谈，向他们展示你的产品，看看他们是否真的想购买。

sentences.text: Now, there are different ways of taking the pressure off of discovery calls.
sentences.zh: 现在，有几种方法可以减轻发现通话的压力。

sentences.text: Uh the way we teach our students is that there's sort of three frames you could use for your discovery calls.
sentences.zh: 我们教给学生的方法是在发现通话中可以使用三种框架。

sentences.text: Frame number one, you could do a market research frame.
sentences.zh: 框架一，你可以使用市场研究框架。

sentences.text: You could go up to your network or to people that you know, and you say, "Hey, um Johnny, uh you know, I'm thinking of starting a business in niche X helping X solve Y problem.
sentences.zh: 你可以去找你的社交圈或认识的人，说：“嘿，约翰尼，我正在考虑在某个领域创业，帮助某类人解决某个问题。”

sentences.text: Would you be open to a quick coffee conversation or a 15-minute call where, you know, I know that this is somewhat relevant to you.
sentences.zh: 你愿意快速喝杯咖啡聊一聊，或者打个15分钟的电话吗？我知道这和你有点关系。

sentences.text: Not trying to sell you anything.
sentences.zh: 不是想向你推销任何东西。

sentences.text: I just really want to understand more about the problem just just so I can do some market research.
sentences.zh: 我只是想更深入地了解这个问题，以便做一些市场研究。

sentences.text: That's a very chill way of doing market research on an offer.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常轻松的方式来做关于某个产品的市场研究。

sentences.text: There's a wonderful book by Rob Fitzpatrick called The Mom Test, which is basically about how to run conversations like this so that you actually get real feedback from people about your business idea.
sentences.zh: 有一本很棒的书，叫《妈妈测试》，作者是罗布·菲茨帕特里克，主要讲如何进行这样的对话，以便从人们那里获得关于你商业想法的真实反馈。

sentences.text: And it's called The Mom Test because it's like your mom will lie to you about about whether your idea is any good.
sentences.zh: 它叫《妈妈测试》，因为就像你妈妈会对你的想法是否靠谱撒谎一样。

sentences.text: Generally, if you ask friends and family and you don't know the process of how to actually pitch them a business idea, they will just lie to you be like, "Oh yeah, that sounds like a good idea."
sentences.zh: 一般来说，如果你问朋友和家人，但不知道如何向他们推销商业想法的过程，他们只会对你撒谎说：“哦，是的，这听起来是个好主意。”

sentences.text: And then actually it sounds like a terrible idea and they're just trying to not hurt your feelings.
sentences.zh: 然后实际上这听起来是个糟糕的主意，他们只是不想伤害你的感情。

sentences.text: So, what you want to do is you want to learn the process for how to have a good market research conversation and then have a bunch of market research conversations.
sentences.zh: 所以，你要做的是学习如何进行良好的市场调研对话，然后进行一系列市场调研对话。

sentences.text: Frame number two you could use is you could use the frame of a free coaching call.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用的第二个框架是免费咨询电话的框架。

sentences.text: So, one of our students in the Lifestyle Business Academy, Kelsey, she helps these tech people get promoted.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在生活方式商业学院的一名学生凯尔西，她帮助这些科技人员获得晋升。

sentences.text: And so, what she did is she posted on LinkedIn basically offering 10 free coaching sessions.
sentences.zh: 她做的是在领英上发帖，基本上提供10次免费咨询。

sentences.text: That did super well.
sentences.zh: 效果非常好。

sentences.text: People a bunch of people signed up for her free coaching calls.
sentences.zh: 很多人报名参加了她的免费咨询电话。

sentences.text: And as a result of the free coaching, a bunch of people spontaneously asked her, "Hey, can I actually work with you on more of a paid basis?"
sentences.zh: 作为免费咨询的结果，很多人自发地问她：“嘿，我能不能以付费的方式与你合作？”

sentences.text: So, she was able to make sales without having to feel salesy about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，她能够在不显得有销售感的情况下完成销售。

sentences.text: And this works if you have genuine skills or expertise to share with someone.
sentences.zh: 如果你有真正的技能或专业知识可以与他人分享，这种方法就有效。

sentences.text: If you're approaching a brand new niche and you have no skills and no experience, then yeah, you kind of need the market research frame.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在进入一个全新的领域，没有任何技能和经验，那么是的，你确实需要市场调研框架。

sentences.text: The the frame of market research is you are doing me a favor by [music] getting on this call with me.
sentences.zh: 市场调研的框架是，你愿意接听这个电话是在帮我一个忙。

sentences.text: And so, you frame it like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你就这样去构建它。

sentences.text: But the frame of a coaching call is that it's it's sort of like a win-win.
sentences.zh: 但教练电话的框架是，这有点像双赢。

sentences.text: Like, "Hey, I've got some experience in the space.
sentences.zh: 比如，“嘿，我在这个领域有一些经验。

sentences.text: Let's hop on a call.
sentences.zh: 我们打个电话吧。

sentences.text: I'd love to help you with your problems and in return I'd love some feedback on this business I'm thinking of starting."
sentences.zh: 我很乐意帮助你解决你的问题，作为回报，我也希望得到一些关于我正在考虑创业的反馈。”

sentences.text: It's a win-win.
sentences.zh: 这是双赢。

sentences.text: But you can only do that if you actually genuinely have some amount of skills or expertise to be able to share.
sentences.zh: 但只有当你真正拥有一些可以分享的技能或专业知识时，你才能这样做。

sentences.text: You don't have to be the world expert in your given niche.
sentences.zh: 你不必成为特定领域的全球专家。

sentences.text: You just need to be a couple of steps ahead of your target audience such that it's actually valuable for them to hop on a call with you.
sentences.zh: 你只需要比你的目标受众领先几步，这样他们与你通话才真正有价值。

sentences.text: And then frame number three that you can [music] do is you can actually just go for a sales call frame.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以使用的第三种框架是直接采用销售电话框架。

sentences.text: Like at one point we were doing interviews for applicants of our Lifestyle Business Academy and I was taking these calls.
sentences.zh: 比如有一次，我们为生活方式商业学院的申请者进行面试，我接听了这些电话。

sentences.text: But I was framing them as interviews because what I was doing in that is I was positioning it that I am the expert and the student is applying for our academy and then I'm doing this interview to see
sentences.zh: 但我把它们框定为面试，因为我在其中所做的是将自己定位为专家，而学生正在申请我们的学院，然后我进行这次面试来看看

sentences.text: if they're the right fit.
sentences.zh: 他们是否合适。

sentences.text: They knew that if they were the right fit, I was going to tell them about the offer, I was going to give them the pricing on the call, but it's not framed as you'll get free coaching from Ali
sentences.zh: 他们知道，如果他们合适，我会告诉他们这个优惠，我会在电话中给他们定价，但这并不是框定为你可以从Ali Abdaal那里获得免费辅导

sentences.text: Abdaal.
It's not framed as, "Hey, I'm starting a business and doing some market research."
sentences.zh: 也不是框定为“嘿，我正在创业，做一些市场调研。”

sentences.text: It's framed as, "Hey, you want into this program?
sentences.zh: 而是框定为“嘿，你想加入这个项目吗？

sentences.text: I'm going to talk to you and see if we're the right fit and if we are, then I'll tell you more details about the program."
sentences.zh: 我会和你谈谈，看看我们是否合适，如果合适，我会告诉你更多关于这个项目的细节。”

sentences.text: It still doesn't have to feel salesy.
sentences.zh: 这仍然不必让人觉得有推销感。

sentences.text: I did like maybe 30 or 40 of these calls and I don't think anyone felt like I was being salesy on them, but it was still a sales frame.
sentences.zh: 我大概打了30到40个这样的电话，我不认为有任何人觉得我在推销，但这仍然是一个销售框架。

sentences.text: [music] And this is what you do if you have confidence in the thing that you're actually selling cuz this is the one that's most likely to get you to actually get customers to give you their money.
sentences.zh: [音乐] 这就是当你对自己实际销售的东西有信心时所做的事情，因为这是最有可能让你真正让顾客付钱给你的方法。

sentences.text: What often students tend to do is they start off in the market research frame, they realize very quickly that like actually they do have skills in the niche and they transition to free coaching calls and then some people
sentences.zh: 学生们通常的做法是，他们从市场调研框架开始，很快意识到自己确实在该领域有技能，然后过渡到免费辅导电话，接着有些人

sentences.text: transition to the sales call frame, you know, once they've landed their first sale and beyond.
sentences.zh: 过渡到销售电话框架，你知道，一旦他们完成了第一笔销售及之后。

sentences.text: But this then helps solve the problem, right?
sentences.zh: 但这有助于解决问题，对吧？

sentences.text: Of like when we don't want to spend bloody ages trying to build a product that no one wants to buy because we are validating it as we go along with our market research calls and maybe our free coaching
sentences.zh: 比如，当我们不想花大量时间构建一个没人想买的产品时，因为我们通过市场调研电话、免费辅导来验证它。

sentences.text: calls and maybe our sales calls.
sentences.zh: 电话，也许还有销售电话。

sentences.text: And as a result, every time we get new data from the market, we are we're getting more insights into is the thing that we are supposedly trying to sell actually solving a problem that someone [music] has?
sentences.zh: 结果，每次我们从市场获得新数据时，我们就能更深入地了解我们试图销售的东西是否真的在解决某人的问题。

sentences.text: Cuz again, the single biggest reason why most businesses in the early days fail is what?
sentences.zh: 因为，大多数企业在早期失败的最大原因是什么？

sentences.text: Firstly, people just don't get started because they're like, "Oh my god, business is scary."
sentences.zh: 首先，人们就是不敢开始，因为他们觉得“天哪，做生意太可怕了”。

sentences.text: Hopefully, this video helps you see the process is not that scary, but secondly, it's that they're trying to sell something that fundamentally no one actually wants to buy.
sentences.zh: 希望这个视频能让你看到这个过程并不可怕，但其次，他们试图销售的东西根本没人想买。

sentences.text: So all this somewhat begs the question of like, "Okay, I've got to have these 10 discovery calls, but like how how do I get people to have calls with me?"
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都引出了一个问题：“好吧，我必须进行10次探索性通话，但我怎么才能让人们和我通话呢？”

sentences.text: And this is where the concept of marketing comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是营销概念发挥作用的地方。

sentences.text: Like how do you let people know about your stuff?
sentences.zh: 比如，你如何让人们了解你的东西？

sentences.text: The word marketing with the word sales feels very scary to people, it doesn't have to feel scary, but broadly, there are a handful of different ways to do this.
sentences.zh: “营销”和“销售”这两个词让人感觉很可怕，其实不必如此，但大致有几种不同的方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.text: Number one is you can and should totally reach out to your existing network.
sentences.zh: 第一，你可以而且应该完全联系你现有的社交网络。

sentences.text: The students in our Lifestyle Business Academy who are succeeding the fastest are the ones who have a network within the space that they are starting a business.
sentences.zh: 在我们的生活方式商业学院中，那些成功最快的学生，是在他们创业的领域内拥有社交网络的人。

sentences.text: So for example, back in the day when I was starting up my my medical school admissions business, on the 2nd of September 2012, this is what I posted on Facebook in the WHSP Westcliff High School for Boys Medical
sentences.zh: 例如，当年我刚开始做医学院入学咨询业务时，2012年9月2日，我在Facebook上的WHSP Westcliff High School for Boys Medical Society小组里发了这个帖子。

sentences.text: Society Facebook group.
sentences.zh: Facebook小组。

sentences.text: Hey guys, at some point in September I'll be running a weekend crash course on the BMAT, most likely in school.
sentences.zh: 嘿，各位，九月份的某个时候，我会在学校里举办一个BMAT周末速成班。

sentences.text: If you're applying to Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial, and or UCL, you'll definitely want to come as the BMAT will be the most important exam of your life and can make or break an application.
sentences.zh: 如果你要申请牛津、剑桥、帝国理工或伦敦大学学院，你绝对想来，因为BMAT将是你人生中最重要的考试，能决定申请的成败。

sentences.text: One day will be dedicated to sections one and three, which are basically about blah blah blah.
sentences.zh: 第一天将专注于第一部分和第三部分，基本上是关于等等等等。

sentences.text: The second day will focus on section two, blah blah blah.
sentences.zh: 第二天将专注于第二部分，等等等等。

sentences.text: Sadly, I am going to have to charge for it cuz I need to make some money for university.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，我得收费，因为我需要为大学挣点钱。

sentences.text: It's probably going to be around 100 pounds for the two days, which is pretty good considering Kaplan costs 300 pounds and sucks.
sentences.zh: 两天大概100英镑，这相当不错了，因为Kaplan要300英镑还很烂。

sentences.text: Anyway, if you're interested, shoot me a message on Facebook and I'll give you more details when the time comes.
sentences.zh: 总之，如果你感兴趣，在Facebook上给我发消息，到时候我会给你更多细节。

sentences.text: This was how I got my first handful of customers for this new business that I was starting.
sentences.zh: 这就是我如何为我正在创办的新业务获得第一批客户的方式。

sentences.text: I just went out to the people I already knew.
sentences.zh: 我只是去找了我已经认识的人。

sentences.text: If I was trying to start a business in like a random niche, like helping dog owners in the Midwest in the US help like walk their dogs, and I was like a teenager in the UK, it's very difficult
sentences.zh: 如果我试图在一个随机的小众领域创业，比如帮助美国中部的狗主人遛狗，而我是英国的一个青少年，那很难

sentences.text: for me to have a network in that space.
sentences.zh: 让我在那个领域有人脉网络。

sentences.text: And so it's hard for me to start a business.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说创业很难。

sentences.text: But if you start a business in a niche where you already have a little bit of a network, life becomes easier.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在一个你已经有一点人脉的小众领域创业，生活就会变得更容易。

sentences.text: You can see this was liked by Manesh Srivastava.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这条被Manesh Srivastava点赞了。

sentences.text: Uh he was actually one of my first customers back when he was like 17 years old.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是我最早的客户之一，当时他才17岁。

sentences.text: And now, or what what is it?
sentences.zh: 而现在，或者是什么？

sentences.text: Like 15 years later, he's actually a neurologist working in Oxford, last time I checked.
sentences.zh: 大约15年后，他实际上是一名在牛津工作的神经科医生，我上次了解的情况是这样。

sentences.text: So, it's, you know, interesting how that works.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这挺有意思的。

sentences.text: This is an example when Alex Hormozi, the famous business guru, was starting his like personal training business.
sentences.zh: 这是一个例子，当Alex Hormozi，那位著名的商业大师，刚开始他的个人训练业务时。

sentences.text: And he's basically saying that like, "Hey, I've got this business where I'm going to help people improve their fitness.
sentences.zh: 他基本上在说：“嘿，我有个业务，可以帮助人们改善他们的健康状况。

sentences.text: If you're interested, drop me a message."
sentences.zh: 如果你感兴趣，给我发条消息。”

sentences.text: And it's very chill.
sentences.zh: 而且非常放松。

sentences.text: It doesn't feel that salesy.
sentences.zh: 感觉没那么推销味。

sentences.text: It feels very authentic, very nice.
sentences.zh: 感觉很真实，很好。

sentences.text: But he's going out to his network on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 但他正在他的Facebook社交圈里推广。

sentences.text: He is known amongst his friends and family and stuff as like the guy who's jacked.
sentences.zh: 他在朋友和家人中被称为那个肌肉发达的家伙。

sentences.text: And so he gets his first few clients for his new business from the people that he already knows.
sentences.zh: 于是，他新业务的第一批客户就来自他认识的人。

sentences.text: This is scary for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这对很多人来说很可怕。

sentences.text: A lot of our students in the Lifestyle Business Academy feel more terrified of telling the people that know them that they're going to start a business compared to random strangers because you're like, "Oh my god, I'm going to
sentences.zh: 在生活方式商业学院，我们很多学生更害怕告诉认识的人自己要创业，而不是告诉陌生人，因为你会想：“天哪，我要

sentences.text: post on LinkedIn or Facebook.
sentences.zh: 在领英或脸书上发帖。

sentences.text: Colleagues are going to see this.
sentences.zh: 同事们会看到这个。

sentences.text: Like, you know, what we try and do is sort of coach, oops, coach people through the process of getting over these fears.
sentences.zh: 我们试图做的是指导人们克服这些恐惧的过程。

sentences.text: So anyway, you reach out to people in your network.
sentences.zh: 所以，你要联系你网络中的人。

sentences.text: And what ultimately happens is you have a DM conversation with them.
sentences.zh: 最终的结果是你和他们进行了一次私信对话。

sentences.text: You exchange a few messages back and forth.
sentences.zh: 你们来回交换了几条信息。

sentences.text: And if they are interested, you get them on your call or a coffee if it's an in-person in-person generally works better, but it can of course just be a Zoom call as well.
sentences.zh: 如果他们感兴趣，你就让他们参加你的电话会议，或者如果是线下见面，喝杯咖啡通常效果更好，但当然也可以是Zoom通话。

sentences.text: That is method number one for getting people into your discovery calls, and is by far the easiest and the quickest and the one that we always recommend.
sentences.zh: 这是让人们进入你的探索电话的第一种方法，也是迄今为止最简单、最快的方法，我们一直推荐这种方法。

sentences.text: Method number two is you start doing content.
sentences.zh: 第二种方法是你开始创作内容。

sentences.text: And back in the day, content used to be hard because you would have to spend years building an audience before you were able to sell anything.
sentences.zh: 在过去，内容创作很难，因为你必须花数年时间建立受众才能销售任何东西。

sentences.text: These days, it's less about social media, it's more about interest media.
sentences.zh: 如今，这更多是关于兴趣媒体，而不是社交媒体。

sentences.text: These days, if you if your content is actually good and is solving a specific problem for a specific person, the algorithms on all of these platforms have gotten so good that it's actually relatively easy if the content is
sentences.zh: 如今，如果你的内容确实很好，并且为特定的人解决了特定问题，所有平台上的算法已经变得非常出色，以至于实际上相对容易——如果内容

sentences.text: good for it to reach a lot of people who are in the target market.
sentences.zh: 好的话——让内容触达目标市场中的大量人群。

sentences.text: Again, we've got some students in our program who have just started posting content and within about two or three weeks of posting every day on LinkedIn, they started to get random strangers DMing them to have conversations with them
sentences.zh: 再次强调，我们项目中有一些学生刚开始发布内容，在LinkedIn上每天发布大约两到三周后，就开始有陌生人私信他们进行对话，

sentences.text: that they were able to then get onto discovery calls.
sentences.zh: 然后他们能够将这些对话转化为探索电话。

sentences.text: The content was also solving the specific problem for the niche.
sentences.zh: 内容也解决了该细分市场的特定问题。

sentences.text: So, let's say my niche is helping like accounting firms automate their onboarding or something like that so that they can save time.
sentences.zh: 假设我的定位是帮助会计事务所自动化客户入职流程之类的事情，这样他们就能节省时间。

sentences.text: The stuff I'm going to be posting on LinkedIn is going to be about that niche.
sentences.zh: 我将在领英上发布的内容都会围绕这个定位。

sentences.text: It's going to be speaking to those accountants.
sentences.zh: 这些内容会针对那些会计师。

sentences.text: I'm it's going to be a post about like how annoying it is that like client onboarding takes so long and here are three tips that you can use to speed it up.
sentences.zh: 我会发一篇帖子，比如讲客户入职流程耗时太长有多烦人，以及你可以用来加快速度的三个技巧。

sentences.text: It's going to be about like how you can use AI in your accounting firm to speed up your operations or stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 还会讲如何在你的会计事务所里使用人工智能来加快运营速度之类的内容。

sentences.text: Random people aren't going to interact with that because they don't like why why would a random person care about like helping accountants save time, but if an accountant who is like is reading that thing, they're like, "Whoa, this
sentences.zh: 随机的人不会与这些内容互动，因为他们为什么会在乎帮助会计师节省时间呢？但如果一个会计师读到那篇文章，他们会觉得，“哇，这

sentences.text: is like directly targeted to me."
sentences.zh: 就是直接针对我的。”

sentences.text: LinkedIn the platform the algorithm recognizes that wait a minute, that person is an accountant.
sentences.zh: 领英这个平台，算法会识别出：等一下，那个人是会计师。

sentences.text: Let's push this post out to similar people like that person.
sentences.zh: 让我们把这篇文章推送给类似的人。

sentences.text: And so now more and more accountants are going to see that post.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，越来越多的会计师会看到那篇文章。

sentences.text: It's never going to go viral because there's not that many accountants out there.
sentences.zh: 它永远不会病毒式传播，因为会计师并没有那么多。

sentences.text: It's not going to get zillions of views, but it might get tens to maybe even hundreds of views from people that are squarely within your target market.
sentences.zh: 它不会获得海量浏览量，但可能会获得几十甚至几百次来自完全属于你目标市场的人的浏览量。

sentences.text: And so that is what we are trying to do with content.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们试图通过内容做的事情。

sentences.text: We are not trying to get famous.
sentences.zh: 我们不是试图出名。

sentences.text: We are trying to become an authority within our niche by posting valuable useful educational stuff that helps people.
sentences.zh: 我们试图通过发布有价值、有用、有教育意义的内容来成为我们领域的权威，从而帮助人们。

sentences.text: As a result of our content, we are also going to be having DM conversations with people.
sentences.zh: 作为我们内容的结果，我们还将与人们进行私信对话。

sentences.text: So, we're going to encourage people to DM us if they want to find out more about working with us or whatever, but also anytime someone likes or comments or engages or follows, we're going to send them a message.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们会鼓励人们私信我们，如果他们想了解更多关于与我们合作或其他事情，而且每当有人点赞、评论、互动或关注时，我们都会给他们发一条消息。

sentences.text: This is why generally I actually recommend people start out on a platform like LinkedIn or Instagram rather than YouTube because you can't DM people on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我通常建议人们从LinkedIn或Instagram这样的平台开始，而不是YouTube，因为在YouTube上你不能私信别人。

sentences.text: It's really hard to make compelling long-form educational YouTube videos.
sentences.zh: 制作引人入胜的长篇教育性YouTube视频非常困难。

sentences.text: It takes absolutely ages.
sentences.zh: 这需要花费很长时间。

sentences.text: Like you got to deal with the editing.
sentences.zh: 比如你得处理剪辑。

sentences.text: Yes, there's AI tools, but it's still drastically easier to post on LinkedIn or Instagram than it is to make YouTube videos.
sentences.zh: 是的，有AI工具，但在LinkedIn或Instagram上发帖仍然比制作YouTube视频容易得多。

sentences.text: So, we have a couple of students in our Lifestyle Business Academy who are doing YouTube.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们的生活方式商业学院里有几个学生在做YouTube。

sentences.text: Um generally those are the ones who took my YouTuber Academy course back in the day anyway.
sentences.zh: 嗯，通常那些是以前参加过我的YouTuber学院课程的人。

sentences.text: And so, they already have the skills of YouTube.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们已经具备了YouTube的技能。

sentences.text: But this is why generally I prefer LinkedIn or Instagram if I was starting today because it's easier to start DM conversations with people.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么如果我现在开始，我通常更喜欢LinkedIn或Instagram，因为更容易与人开始私信对话。

sentences.text: At this point you might be like, "What?
sentences.zh: 此时你可能会想：“什么？”

sentences.text: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.text: Why do I have to chat to so many people?"
sentences.zh: 为什么我必须和这么多人聊天？”

sentences.text: Cuz what we all want, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我们大家都想要，对吧？

sentences.text: Is we we want the passive income dream.
sentences.zh: 我们想要被动收入的梦想。

sentences.text: We want the idea of like, "Oh man, I'm just going to wake up to some Stripe notifications.
sentences.zh: 我们想要这样的想法：“哦，天哪，我醒来就会看到一些Stripe通知。

sentences.text: It's going to be sick."
sentences.zh: 那会很棒。”

sentences.text: But in reality, like that's just not how the world works anymore.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，世界已经不再是这样了。

sentences.text: Um it kind of does if you're selling like super cheap things, but given that it's a lot easier to build a business selling expensive things, we're going to need to have conversations with people.
sentences.zh: 如果你卖的是非常便宜的东西，那还有点可能，但鉴于卖昂贵的东西更容易建立业务，我们将需要与人进行对话。

sentences.text: We're going to probably need to have calls with people.
sentences.zh: 我们可能还需要与人通电话。

sentences.text: And that is amazing, especially in the early days where we are still validating that there is a market for the thing that we are thinking of maybe selling.
sentences.zh: 这非常棒，尤其是在早期阶段，我们还在验证我们可能想卖的东西是否有市场。

sentences.text: The third source of leads to our discovery call is strangers.
sentences.zh: 引导到我们发现通话的第三个潜在客户来源是陌生人。

sentences.text: [music] Now, there's a few different ways to talk to strangers.
sentences.zh: [音乐] 现在，有几种不同的方式与陌生人交谈。

sentences.text: Um the one I like the least is cold outreach.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我最不喜欢的是冷接触。

sentences.text: We do have some students who are doing it with some level of success, but like cold outreach, cold emails, cold DMing people, uh that's like a volume game.
sentences.zh: 我们确实有一些学生在这方面取得了一定程度的成功，但像冷接触、冷邮件、冷私信，那是一种数量游戏。

sentences.text: It's a numbers game.
sentences.zh: 这是一个数字游戏。

sentences.text: I've been going through Charlie Morgan stuff.
sentences.zh: 我一直在研究查理·摩根的东西。

sentences.text: He specializes in cold outreach, and it's just like you got to send hundreds of messages and face rejection every single day, and you feel like a bit of a spammer because you're like sending cold emails and doing cold
sentences.zh: 他专门从事冷接触，就是你必须发送数百条信息，每天面对拒绝，感觉自己有点像垃圾邮件发送者，因为你发送冷邮件和进行冷电话。

sentences.text: calling and stuff.
sentences.zh: 打电话之类的事情。

sentences.text: Uh that doesn't seem like my idea of fun.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那似乎不是我的乐趣所在。

sentences.text: But there are other ways of reaching out to strangers.
sentences.zh: 但还有其他方式可以接触陌生人。

sentences.text: So, one thing is you can join and post in communities.
sentences.zh: 所以，一件事是你可以在社区中发帖和加入。

sentences.text: These could be online communities.
sentences.zh: 这些可能是线上社区。

sentences.text: These could be offline communities.
sentences.zh: 这些可能是线下社区。

sentences.text: A good offline example is one of our students, Ronke.
sentences.zh: 一个很好的线下例子是我们的一个学生，Ronke。

sentences.text: She's a doctor, and her offer is helping uh corporations deal with employee burnout so that they can save like 100k a year in terms of like um staff retention and medical expenses and stuff.
sentences.zh: 她是一名医生，她的服务是帮助企业应对员工倦怠，这样他们每年可以在员工保留和医疗费用等方面节省大约10万美元。

sentences.text: And she realized that she didn't know that many people in her existing network who were like heads of HR and CEOs of big corporations.
sentences.zh: 她意识到，在她现有的社交圈中，她并不认识很多大公司的人力资源主管和CEO。

sentences.text: So, what she did is she went to some real-life networking events in London where those people hung out.
sentences.zh: 所以，她做的是去伦敦的一些真实社交活动，那些地方是那些人常去的。

sentences.text: And so, she spoke to them, she was a normal person, she was friendly, she got some business cards, and was then able to have conversations with those people afterwards by following up on LinkedIn and then get some of
